correctness.rationale: For selected a in class i its neighborhood in B is B\B_i. Distinct selected vertices in one class have equal signatures, so at most one per class. Chosen vertices from two singleton parts also collide; hence at most one singleton may be selected. Mutual domination supplies exactly the p>=2 product, p=1 s>=2 boundary and p=0 boundary. Reapplying constraints after exchanging sides requires each nonsingleton class size two, s<=2, and listed p/s cases for double-LD. Independent direct bitmask enumeration tested all 41 unordered multipartite profiles with 2..5 classes of sizes <=3 and <=10 total vertices, matching both coefficient vectors. This supports but does not prove the universal formulas.
